why: `e as T` checks nothing at run time (the emit drops it). The proof lane read a narrowing assertion as an uninterpreted conversion into T, then read T's operations exactly, so `x as number` on a string | number, `x as string` on unknown, `JSON.parse(s) as { a: number }`, an any parameter in a number slot and a Wide literal narrowed to Mode before an exhaustive switch were each proved equal to a candidate that differs on a value of another type ("a" + 0 is "a0"). Each is now refused as type-assertion by the lint and the translator through one predicate (common.mjs typeAssertion): lane B witnesses the other type, lane A says nothing (parent against itself PASS-bounded). An assertion to a supertype (widen) and from a literal into its union (rank) pass the value through with its real type and are proved, beside a unit without one (plain).
